prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a bedroom with a close left wall (~0.5–1.5 m), a low mattress directly in front and below the camera wearer (~0.8–2.5 m) topped with a turquoise blanket and a toy (~1.2–1.5 m away, ~0.3 m left of the child), a crib to the right (~1.2–2.0 m), and a receding corner and hallway behind (>3 m). In frame 1 the child's head is barely visible at the bottom edge (<0.6 m), and from frames 2 to 5 the child moves onto the mattress from ~0.5 m to ~0.9 m directly in front of the camera wearer, turning from facing away toward the bed in frame 2 to facing and looking toward the camera wearer while sitting down in frames 3–5, while a second person's legs or feet appear at the bottom-left edge (~0.7–1.0 m) in frames 2–5. The near edge of the bed, the child, and the left wall are within arm's reach of the camera wearer (<0.8 m), while the turquoise blanket and yellow-and-red toy on the bed are within arm's reach of the child, who partially occludes the middle of the bed and blanket while the crib is progressively cut off at the right border as the camera turns left and tilts down. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouette of the child and the crib rails from the similarly toned background bedding and walls, and clarifies the continuous surface slope of the mattress and wall corners. However, the map is unreliable in the far background where the open doorway and corner walls collapse into uniform black, and in frame 2 where the child's torso is over-saturated into a flat white blob lacking 3D surface detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the main bed surface (~0.8–2.5 m in front and below the camera wearer) and the foreground child (~0.5–0.9 m in front, slightly right of center), along with the yellow-and-red toy (~1.2–1.5 m away, ~0.3 m to the child's left on the blanket) and a second person's lower limb at the bottom-left edge (~0.8 m away in frame 3). Across the 5 frames, the segmented bed shifts toward the center-right as the camera wearer approaches and looks down, while the child's mask rises from the bottom edge in frame 2 (facing away) and shifts slightly backward onto the bed in frames 3–5 while turning to face toward the camera wearer, with both the child and near bed edge within the camera wearer's arm's reach and the toy and blanket within the child's arm's reach. The child's mask occludes the central-right portion of the bed mask in frames 2–5, while the lower legs of the child and the person on the far left are partly out of view at the bottom and left frame borders. Unlike the RGB image where the dark-clothed and blurred child blends into the dark blue blanket in frames 2–3, the segmentation masks provide sharp outer boundaries separating the child's silhouette from the bedding. However, the map is unreliable because it misses the crib, walls, and drawers entirely, leaves large unlabelled black holes inside the bed mask where the turquoise blanket lies, mislabels the plastic toy as a 'teddy bear' (frames 2, 3, 5) or 'dog' (frame 3), and misses the child in frame 1 and the left-side person in frames 2, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D keypoints on a black background only in frames 3, 4, and 5, showing the child positioned in the lower-right foreground (~0.7–0.9 m in front of and below the camera wearer) sitting on the unrendered bed surface. In frame 3, only a magenta hand skeleton is detected near the bottom center (~0.6 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) where the child's left hand rests on the mattress, while frames 4 and 5 show a yellow full-body skeleton with torso, hips, knees, and arms supported on the bed within arm's reach of the adjacent blanket and toy (~0.3 m to the left). Across frames 4 and 5, the skeleton's bilateral shoulder and hip alignment and clustered facial keypoints at the top confirm that the child faces and looks toward the camera wearer while shifting slightly further back on the mattress, with the lower legs cropped out of view at the bottom border in frame 4 and the left arm self-occluded or folded in frame 5. The pose map makes the exact joint articulations—such as the wide-set knees, hip angle, and weight-bearing arms on the mattress—explicit despite the heavy privacy blur and dark lighting on the child in the RGB strip. However, it is completely unreliable in frames 1 and 2 where no skeletons are detected at all, misses the child's head and torso in frame 3, never detects the second person on the bottom left, and collapses the facial keypoints in frames 4–5 into an offset cluster above the left shoulder.
